scale_008:n1.prompt:
You are helping me draft interview stage definitions per role type, as part of building our structured hiring pipeline. This is a design-preparation task only: an HR leader must review and finalize before anything is applied.

First, ask me for anything you need that's missing, such as: (1) our current or planned open role types/categories (e.g., Engineering, Sales, Customer Support, Marketing, People Ops, Executive/Leadership), (2) any existing interview stages we already use, (3) company size/stage and hiring volume, and (4) whether we have specific legal/fairness constraints (e.g., structured scoring requirements, jurisdictions with hiring regulations).

Then, for each role type, draft a proposed interview pipeline including: recommended number of stages, purpose of each stage (e.g., recruiter screen, hiring manager screen, technical/skills assessment, panel interview, culture/values interview, reference check), suggested interviewers or interviewer roles per stage, estimated time per stage, and a note on where structured scorecards and diversity-tracking checkpoints would plug in. Keep the stages consistent in format across role types so they can later be loaded into whatever applicant tracking system we use (do not assume or name a specific vendor).

Organize the output as a clear table or structured document, one per role type, with a short rationale for why each stage was included (rigor, fairness, role-specific need). Flag any stage that may raise legal or fairness concerns (e.g., unstructured panel interviews) so the human reviewer can address it.

When done, present the full draft set of role-type interview stage definitions to me in a clean, reviewable format, summarize key design tradeoffs you made, and then stop for human sign-off — do not finalize, publish, or load these stages into any system yourself.

scale_008:n2.prompt:
You are helping me create job postings in {{vendor}}, our applicant-tracking vendor, as part of building a multi-role hiring pipeline. Before starting, ask me for anything you don't already have: (1) my {{vendor}} account/workspace details and confirmation you should use my configured credentials, (2) the list of open roles (title, department, location, employment type, seniority), (3) job description content or bullet points for each role, (4) any custom application questions, knockout rules, or EEOC/demographic data collection I want enabled, (5) my careers-page domain/branding preferences, and (6) which job boards (e.g. LinkedIn, Indeed, aggregators) I want each posting distributed to, including any sponsored-post budget.

Once you have these inputs, draft each job posting fully: title, description, custom questions, knockout rules, compliant EEOC/demographic fields, careers-page branding settings, and the target job-board distribution list. Use the {{vendor}} API operations for creating a company offer (the 'create offer' endpoint) and for listing published jobs (the 'get offers' endpoint) to prepare and verify these drafts, or use the dashboard equivalents if the API doesn't support a field. Do not publish anything live — leave postings in draft/unpublished status.

When done, give me a summary per role showing: draft status, description snippet, custom questions/knockout rules configured, EEOC/demographic fields included, careers-page publish target, and job-board fan-out plan. Flag any fields you couldn't set via API and note what manual dashboard step would be needed.

Because a human must explicitly approve before these postings go live, do not publish, sponsor, or fan out any posting yourself — stop for human sign-off once drafts and the summary are ready.

scale_008:n3.prompt:
You are helping me configure scorecard templates in {{vendor}}, our applicant-tracking platform, as part of building a structured multi-role hiring pipeline. This step requires my explicit approval before any changes go live, so your job is to PREPARE everything and then stop.

First, ask me for anything you need that isn't already available: which open roles/job families need scorecards, the interview stages per role, the key attributes/competencies to rate at each stage, per-interviewer focus areas (e.g., technical depth, culture add, communication), and whether we want demographic-blind review options enabled for DEI tracking.

Then, using your configured credentials to access {{vendor}} (via its dashboard or documented API as appropriate), do the following:
1. Draft a scorecard template per role/stage combination, listing the defined attributes, a focused rubric per interviewer role, and a consistent rating scale so results are comparable across candidates.
2. Map each scorecard to the correct interview plan stage and question bank entries where they already exist.
3. Prepare configuration for structured feedback ordering (so early reviewers don't bias later ones) and note where demographic-blind review can be toggled on.
4. Set up or confirm DEI reporting fields tied to the funnel so scorecard data feeds diversity tracking.
5. Compile a clear summary checklist showing: roles covered, stages covered, attributes per scorecard, interviewer assignments, and any bias-reduction settings staged (not yet applied).

Do not submit, publish, or apply these scorecard templates in {{vendor}} — only prepare drafts and pre-filled configuration values. When the checklist and draft templates are ready, present them to me and stop for human sign-off before any changes are applied.

scale_008:n4.prompt:
You are helping me configure the offer approval workflow inside {{vendor}}, our applicant-tracking system, as part of building a structured, multi-role hiring pipeline. If you don't already have it, ask me for: (1) my {{vendor}} account/domain details, (2) the roles and hiring managers who should sit in each approval chain (e.g., recruiter → hiring manager → finance → exec), and (3) any offer letter templates with dynamic fields (salary, start date, title) we want used.

Using my configured credentials, please:
1. Review current offer settings in {{vendor}} and draft a configurable approval chain per role/level, matching the approvers I give you.
2. Prepare or update offer letter templates with the required dynamic fields and confirm e-signature routing is attached to the final approval step.
3. Use the {{vendor}} API call GET /candidates/:id/offer to pull a sample candidate's latest offer so we can verify the approval routing and template fields render correctly before anything goes live.
4. Compile a summary showing: the proposed approval chain(s) per role, the offer template(s) with fields populated from the sample candidate, and where e-signature triggers in the flow.
5. Flag anything that looks misconfigured (missing approver, broken dynamic field, no e-signature step).

Do not activate the workflow, send any offer, or submit approval chain changes as live in {{vendor}} — this requires a human explicitly approves before changes are applied. Present the drafted approval chain, templates, and sample offer review as a checklist and then stop for human sign-off.

Report back with: the approval chain structure per role, the template/field mapping, the sample offer output from the API call, and a clear list of what still needs my review or approval before going live.

scale_008:n5.prompt:
You are helping me connect {{vendor}} for interview scheduling as part of our hiring pipeline build-out. Before starting, ask me for: (1) my company domain/workspace name for {{vendor}}, (2) which calendar account(s) should be connected (e.g. company email/calendar), (3) the interview event types we need (e.g. 'Recruiter Screen', 'Hiring Manager Interview', 'Panel Interview'), including desired durations, locations (video link vs phone), and any custom screening questions per event type, and (4) which downstream systems (ATS/CRM, Zapier, or our own tooling) should receive booking notifications via webhook.

Using your configured credentials, please:
1. Navigate to {{vendor}}'s dashboard and begin the calendar connection flow.
2. Prepare the OAuth authorization request that would grant {{vendor}} access to the specified calendar/email account, but do NOT complete or approve the authorization grant yourself — this remains a human step because it involves data-governance decisions about calendar/email access.
3. Draft the configuration for each event type (name, duration, location, custom questions, confirmation/reminder rules) so it's ready to create once access is approved.
4. Draft the webhook/integration setup instructions (what events to subscribe to — created, rescheduled, canceled — and which endpoint or automation tool, e.g. Zapier, should receive them) as a checklist, without submitting them.
5. Compile a summary checklist showing: the account to be connected, all proposed event types with their settings, and the proposed webhook/integration targets.

Done looks like: a complete, human-readable configuration package (calendar account, event types, webhook targets) ready for review, with the OAuth grant screen reached but not confirmed. Please explicitly stop for human sign-off before finalizing the calendar authorization or activating any webhook integration. Report back with the full checklist, any screens you reached but did not submit, and a clear note on what requires my explicit approval.

scale_008:n6.prompt:
You are helping me configure hiring channels in {{vendor}}, our team-chat tool, as part of building a structured hiring pipeline. This step requires my explicit approval before any changes are applied to our workspace — do not apply anything live.

First, ask me for any missing inputs you need: our {{vendor}} workspace/organization name, the list of open roles or departments we're hiring for (e.g., Engineering, Sales, Design), naming convention preference for channels (e.g., hiring-<role> or interviews-<role>), who should be members (recruiters, hiring managers, interviewers), whether we want separate private channels per role or one shared hiring channel, and whether any external partners (agencies, contractors) need guest/limited access to specific channels.

Using this information, prepare a complete plan: a list of proposed channels with names, public/private setting, and initial member list; a note on which channels (if any) need guest-account or shared-channel access for external partners; and a shortlist of relevant prebuilt integrations from {{vendor}}'s app directory (e.g., calendar scheduling, ATS notifications, scorecard reminders) that could be installed to support the hiring workflow. If our tooling includes command-line access, you may draft the exact command to initialize a new {{vendor}} app/project via its CLI create command, but do not execute it.

Present this full plan — channel list, membership, privacy settings, guest access notes, and integration recommendations — as a clear checklist for my review. Do not create channels, invite members, install integrations, or run any commands. Stop for human sign-off once the plan is ready, and report back with the checklist plus any open questions I need to resolve before approving.

scale_008:n7.prompt:
You are helping me set up diversity tracking in {{vendor}}, our applicant-tracking system, as part of building a structured hiring pipeline. This change requires my explicit sign-off before anything goes live, so you must prepare everything and then stop.

First, ask me for anything you need: my {{vendor}} login/workspace details (use my configured credentials only), which open roles/job families to configure, and whether we have existing EEOC/demographic question language we're required to use, or whether you should draft standard, compliant EEOC/voluntary self-identification questions for our jurisdiction.

Then, in {{vendor}}, prepare (but do not publish or activate) the following:
1. Draft application form updates adding compliant, voluntary EEOC/demographic data collection fields, clearly marked optional and separated from the evaluation criteria used by hiring managers.
2. Configure (in draft/staged form) demographic-blind or anonymized review settings if the platform supports them, so reviewers can optionally see redacted candidate info during initial screens.
3. Set up structured feedback ordering so scorecards are submitted before interviewers can see others' feedback, reducing anchoring bias.
4. Draft a DEI funnel report configuration showing stage conversion, time-to-hire, source effectiveness, and offer-accept rates broken out by demographic categories, role, and team.
5. Compile a summary checklist of all proposed configuration changes, including exact form field wording, review setting toggles, and report definitions.

Do not publish forms, change live review settings, or activate reporting dashboards. Present the full checklist and drafted content to me for review, and clearly state that this remains pending my explicit approval — stop for human sign-off before applying any changes.

Report back with: the drafted EEOC/demographic questions, the bias-reduction settings you configured in draft, the DEI report structure, and a clear list of what will change once I approve.
